subject: Feedback license execution and IP scope — proposed path & timing
messages:
From: Amir Khan <amir.khan@bluevista.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
Cc: sophie.liao@bluevista.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redlines on MSA & Order Form — training use + output title

Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We reviewed the MSA and order form with our legal team and attached a set of redlines focused on two items: (1) ownership of model outputs and downstream productization rights and (2) any implicit consent for model retraining / use of our data for improving models.

High level asks from our side:
- BlueVista must retain title to any productized output that is a derivative of our proprietary prompts/datasets.
- No training or model tuning with customer data without explicit opt-in per contract and an auditable declaration of what was used.
- Feedback we share via support channels should be handled under a narrow feedback license limited to bug fixes and service improvements (no commercial retraining).

We attached the redline file (BlueVista_Redlines_v1.docx) and added inline comments. Can you confirm how Redwood typically handles: telemetry/usage logs, prefix caching, and engineered prompt leakage risk?

Best,
Amir Khan
Head of Platform & Partnerships
BlueVista Systems

---Attachment: BlueVista_Redlines_v1.docx (docx, 85KB)---

From: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
To: Amir Khan <amir.khan@bluevista.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines on MSA & Order Form — training use + output title

Amir — thank you for the detailed redlines and the clear bullets. I’ve looped in Ben (contracts) and Monica (CS/ops) so we can respond decisively. I’ve skimmed the doc and highlighted three immediate clarifications we can provide quickly:

1) Runtime telemetry: we can provide a telemetry export for your account with request-level metadata (non-PII) and a log of caching hits for a 90-day retention window; we’ve noted an action to confirm retention period in writing.

2) Prefix/KV cache leakage: our runtime isolates customer KV caches; we do not share KV across accounts. Monica will include a short technical note on guardrails and what we can attest to in the MSA.

3) Training opt-in: Redwood’s standard position is opt-out by default for hosted service data minimization, but we can offer an express opt-in clause (customer-managed decision) for any explicit retraining/finetune usage and an associated commercial term. Ben — can you take point on a proposed clause that preserves BlueVista’s title carveout but allows Redwood to use anonymized telemetry for product quality improvements under a narrow feedback license?

Amir — we’ll return a redline response with track changes and a short summary in 2 business days. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the doc line-by-line.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Direct: +1 415 555 0182

From: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
To: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com, Amir Khan <amir.khan@bluevista.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 15 May 2029 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Redlines on MSA & Order Form — training use + output title

Amir / Naomi,

I reviewed BlueVista_Redlines_v1 and sketched language that I think narrows the feedback license while preserving Redwood’s ability to operate and improve the hosted service. Attached is Redwood_response_trackchanges.docx with inline edits; summary below:

- Output title: propose a split approach — customer owns "Derivative Product Outputs" defined as outputs that (i) materially incorporate the customer’s proprietary dataset, and (ii) are productized and distributed by the customer. For all other generated outputs, Redwood grants the customer a broad license to use in their business. This preserves customer productization rights while avoiding assignment of Redwood’s general model outputs.

- Training/data use: insert an explicit opt-in checkbox for retraining/finetuning on customer data. By default, telemetry and aggregated non-identifying usage metrics may be used to improve Redwood’s models, but any dataset-level ingestion for model training requires written opt-in and commensurate commercial terms.

- Feedback license: limit to "bug fixes, service improvements, and performance tuning" and expressly exclude using feedback as training material for revenue-generating base model retraining unless opt-in. Also propose an audit right limited to access logs tied to the customer’s dataset for compliance review.

Monica — please attach a one-page tech note describing our cache isolation, options for on-prem/private deployments (if BlueVista needs absolute separation), and telemetry export formats.

Amir — I can hop on a call to walk these edits; Naomi, please advise timing for your commercial counterpart.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
---Attachment: Redwood_response_trackchanges.docx (docx, 62KB)---

From: Amir Khan <amir.khan@bluevista.com>

Subject: Re: Redlines on MSA & Order Form — training use + output title

Ben / Naomi — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear structure in your proposed edits. Our counsel reviewed Redwood_response_trackchanges.docx and had two follow-ups:

1) The proposed definition of "Derivative Product Outputs" looks promising, but BlueVista needs an explicit carveout for outputs that incorporate our trademarked prompts or data schemas even if not materially transformed — can we add a short list-based exception in the definition?

2) On telemetry: we prefer a 180-day rolling export window for request logs and a clause that Redwood will retain export copies for 30 days post-request to allow for transactional reconciliation.

We’d also like to see sample wording for the opt-in button/check box in the order form (i.e., the UI text that commits to retraining) so our procurement team can triage internally.

If possible, we’d like a redline-ready doc by Friday EOD so our procurement can review over the weekend. Otherwise, propose a call Friday morning.

Regards,
Amir

We can provide alternate shorter copy if you need a single-line checkbox.

Deliverable timeline: Ben + Monica will circulate a redline-ready package (tracked changes + redlines_summary.pdf) by Fri EOD PT (today). If that slips, we’ll take the 9:00 AM PT corridor for a 30-minute call — Naomi to confirm room.
